title: Zero-test preservation for zero
statement: Let a nondeterministic register program have a state $l$ whose instruction branches on whether register $r$ is zero, with successor states $l_1$ for zero and $l_0$ for nonzero. If the current configuration $(l,v,	ext{no answer})$ satisfies the guard, register $r$ is zero, and the configuration $(l_1,v,	ext{no answer})$ has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $p$, then $(l,v,	ext{no answer})$ has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $p$.
